Restart identity: terminating and relaunching the model changed the replica address (127.0.0.1:62147 to 127.0.0.1:63318) while 57 other identifiers stayed the same. That is a usable restart signal; candidate B had none in its API and only process_start_time_seconds in /metrics.

Negative test 1: registering the same model_name with a different context_length was refused with HTTP 400 (already registered); a second name over the same weights was accepted and kept separate. The candidate does not merge two profiles under one alias.

Negative test 2 did not run: the second model_uid failed with a Windows paging-file error before any model was loaded, on a host with 31.8 GiB RAM and 5.7 GiB free. The first model kept serving and VRAM was unchanged, so whether the cluster counts one capacity or two remains unobserved.

Authentication: xinference 3.4.0 authenticates by default, which its documentation describes as opt-in. With the default, /v1/models, /v1/model_registrations/LLM, /v1/workers and /v1/supervisor all return 401 with a WWW-Authenticate challenge, and only /v1/cluster/auth and /v1/admin/setup/status answer. One environment variable, XINFERENCE_AUTH_ADVANCED=0, removes all authentication; the measurements in steps 1-3 were taken in that state because the default path requires creating an administrator account.

Deployment: installing xinference==3.4.0 replaced the CUDA torch wheel with torch 2.14.0+cpu, after which the cluster reported gpu_count 0 and refused to launch on GPU. Reinstalling torch 2.14.0+cu130 fixed it. An operator following the obvious install order gets a CPU-only cluster with no warning.

Deployment: the launch path symlinks the weights into its cache and failed with the Windows symlink privilege error (WinError 1314 / 'A required privilege is not held by the client'). A directory junction at the same path needs no privilege change and the launch then succeeded.
The server logs a pre-launch VRAM check (Pre-launch VRAM low ... free_ratio=0.79), so the candidate has an admission signal of its own; this is carried into EV05.

observations: Step 1. The runtime would not start at all under Docker Desktop / WSL2 until VLLM_WSL2_ENABLE_PIN_MEMORY=1 was set: vLLM 0.29.0 disables pinned host memory on WSL2 by default while its V2 GPU model runner requires UVA buffers, so the engine core died with 'UVA is not available'. Root cause and fix in .brain/rca/RCA-2026-09-21-vllm-wsl2-uva.md.

Step 2. No probed endpoint exposed a physical GPU UUID. nvidia-smi on the Windows host matched zero runtime processes because WSL2 GPU paravirtualisation hides them; nvidia-smi inside the container reported GPU-38430611-f42d-0296-a887-d75649b21f25, which equals the UUID already recorded for environment.control_host, and listed the EngineCore pid 131 with process_name '[Not Found]' and used memory '[N/A]'. PRP can therefore join a runtime to a physical GPU only from inside the container, and cannot obtain per-process GPU memory on this substrate.

Step 2. The authenticated model listing exposes no model revision: it returns id, root, max_model_len, owned_by, created and a permission block, so PRP cannot verify from the API that the runtime serves shared_revision ce0a741. The served artifact was instead verified out of band before launch: tokenizer.json sha256 aeb13307a71acd8fe81861d94ad54ab689df773318809eed3cbe794b4492dae4 and chat_template.jinja sha256 64f85b198065d0fba2a81f37e10ed68161ce2c19a754c7100e67e0ca2ee9c326 both match the pinned values, and the two safetensors shards total 8044982000 bytes (7.49 GiB).

Step 2 and step 3, corrected reading. data[0].created and permission[0].id are NOT a restart epoch and NOT runtime identity: three consecutive /v1/models calls against one origin returned three different modelperm-* values, and created tracks the wall clock at request time. Client-visible endings once HTTP 200 is sent: a finish_reason means finished; an in-stream error object means failed (seen on the engine kill); a stream that stops with neither (seen on a restart) or a lost connection tells the client nothing about how far compute got. The HTTP status never carries the failure on a started stream.
